name: ACME Industries
title: Analysts are warming up to ACME. Should you?
dek: Fifteen analysts follow ACME, and most of them just raised their targets. We check whether the numbers back them up.
news: Analysts raise targets after a strong Q1
₹85 Cr payment from a utility is overdue

p: The NIFTY 50 is near its highs and Indian funds keep buying every dip, even as foreign investors sell. Capital goods remain one of the market's favourite corners.

Analysts raised their average ACME target by 9% to ₹1,420 after a strong first quarter. 11 of the 15 are positive, 3 are neutral and 1 is negative, and they now expect profit to grow about 18% this year.
The one blemish: a state utility is late paying ₹85 crore. ACME says the money should arrive by December.

The chart has been stuck below ₹1,225 since July, so the stock needs a clean break above that line to start its next leg up. The business itself looks solid, with **profit growing faster than sales**.
A good company waiting for a breakout. The longer-term signals are bullish; the short-term picture turns clearly bullish only on a close above ₹1,225.

name: ACME Industries
title: ACME's first quarter: profit up 20%, and the orders keep coming
dek: Sales grew 17% and margins improved. Here's what the results mean for the stock.

p: ACME's sales rose 17% to ₹1,560 crore in April to June, and profit grew 20% to ₹158 crore. It kept 15.7 paise of every rupee of sales as operating profit, more than a year ago, and beat what analysts expected by 3.1%.
The board also approved a final dividend of ₹7.50 a share.
sections.quote: Profit growing faster than sales is the sign of a business getting more efficient.

p: The shares jumped 4.6% on the day before giving some of it back. The price is now testing ₹1,221, a level where sellers showed up before.
Strong numbers that support the long-term case. The short-term move depends on getting past ₹1,221.

name: ACME Industries
title: A ₹310 crore export order: ACME's quiet push abroad
dek: A Middle East grid operator has picked ACME. Exports are becoming a bigger part of the story.
news: ₹310 Cr export order from the Middle East

p: ACME won a ₹310 crore order from a grid operator in the Middle East. Exports now make up 28% of its sales.
Selling abroad spreads ACME's risk. It relies less on Indian government orders, which make up 38% of its book and can be slow to pay.
A steady stream of orders keeps the medium-term view positive. For the long term we'd like to see the price cheaper compared with profit.

name: Orbit Engineering
title: Orbit Engineering at a record. Is the uptrend still intact?
dek: The sector's largest company keeps climbing. We weigh a strong trend against a rich price.

p: Government spending on power grids and railways has lifted the whole capital goods sector this year, and the biggest names have led the way.

Orbit's price has risen from about ₹2,210 a year ago to near ₹2,940, and it trades above all its main averages. After such a run the next few weeks could be choppy, but **the trend for the months ahead is still up**.
A quality leader. The signals are bullish for the months ahead and neutral for the next few weeks, after a long run.

name: Nova Machines
title: Nova Machines keeps sliding. What would make it turn?
dek: While its sector rallies, this small cap has drifted lower for months. Here's what to watch.

p: Nova's price has slipped from about ₹780 in April 2025 to below ₹670, even as other capital goods makers hit records. The trend is down and **each bounce has faded**.

items: A close back above its 200-day average
Bigger orders in the next results
Big investors adding shares, not cutting them

p: The short-term signal is bearish and the longer view neutral. A close above the 200-day average would be the first sign of a turn.
